rules: 1 all-in crypto pick per day, 100% deployed
Spot crypto only (BTC, ETH, SOL, and other liquid coins on Robinhood)
Rotate each 6:45am CT run — sell yesterday, buy today's best
Hard stop at entry; leverage conviction, protect downside

positions.name: Bitcoin
positions.catalyst: I AM STAYING IN BITCOIN, AND THE MOST IMPORTANT REASON IS A RULE I WROTE FOR MYSELF YESTERDAY. In yesterday's risk note, after flipping BTC -> ETH -> BTC inside eleven hours and burning ~70bps, I wrote this down verbatim: 'If I find myself flipping between the same two coins a third time this week, the problem is my process, not the market.' Today the tape hands me exactly that temptation. ETH is the strongest name on an eleven-coin board (-0.75% vs BTC -1.34%), the ETH/BTC cross expanded back from 0.0314712 to 0.0316602, and U.S. spot ETH ETFs took +$34.7M on Wednesday while spot BTC ETFs SHED $167M. Three days ago that exact bundle of facts is what moved me into ETH. I am not acting on it, because a 59-basis-point one-day spread is smaller than moves I have already ruled insufficient, and because a rule that only binds when it is convenient is not a rule. THE TAPE IS RISK-OFF ACROSS THE ENTIRE BOARD, WHICH IS THE ACTUAL SIGNAL. 24h to 2026-09-10T10:53:55Z: ETH -0.75%, BTC -1.34%, LINK -2.15%, SOL -2.49%, AVAX -2.50%, ADA -2.52%, LTC -2.95%, XRP -3.14%, AAVE -4.55%, DOGE -5.84%, DOT -6.74%. ELEVEN OF ELEVEN RED. Yesterday BTC was the only green name; today nothing is green. When every asset in a universe moves the same direction, cross-sectional selection is worth very little and the only decision that carries real expected value is how much beta to hold. My mandate says it directly: on low-edge days favor the liquid majors. This is a low-edge day and I am going to treat it as one instead of manufacturing conviction. THE BINARY IS TOMORROW MORNING AND I AM 100% DEPLOYED INTO IT NO MATTER WHAT. August CPI prints Friday 9/11; FOMC decides 9/15-16 with rate-hike odds at ~57% on fed funds futures and ~66% on CME FedWatch, up from 34.8% in late August after August payrolls came in at 162,000 with unemployment steady at 4.1%. The ECB is priced at 100% for a 25bp hike TODAY. This is a tightening-repricing tape, and the board's uniform red is that repricing happening in front of me. A book that must be all-in cannot dodge the event; it can only choose the seat with the least gap risk and the deepest liquidity to exit through. That seat is Bitcoin. MY PRE-REGISTERED INVALIDATION HAS NOT FIRED, AND I CHECKED IT RATHER THAN ASSUMING. I wrote yesterday that the trade ends if 'weekly U.S. spot BTC ETF flows turn NET NEGATIVE.' Wednesday 9/9 was -$167M — a single red day arriving on the back of the strongest three-week inflow run of 2026 at roughly $3.8B. One day is a pause in a run, not the death of one. The second invalidation — dominance below 57% with the Altcoin Season Index recovering above 50 — has not fired either; alts are down 2.5% to 6.7% today, which is dominance rising, not falling. I do not get to exit on a condition I did not write, and I do not get to ignore one I did. WHY NOT ROTATE TO THE ONE ASSET WITH POSITIVE INSTITUTIONAL FLOW. XRP was the standout on 9/9: fresh ETF inflows while BTC, ETH and SOL funds all bled. That is a real divergence and it is the sixth session I have passed on XRP. The reason is that the flow did not show up in the price — XRP is -3.14% over 24h, the fourth-worst name on the board. Flow that the tape refuses to pay for is not a catalyst, it is a hope. The CLARITY Act remains undated into Q4, unchanged for six sessions.
positions.driver: Closed BTC at 77,870.42 (canonical live, asOf 2026-09-10T10:53:55.014Z) vs entry 78,923.39 for -160.59 (-1.33%) on 0.152508 units over a one-day hold. Book rolls 12,036.47 -> 11,875.88, still +18.8% on the $10,000 inception. Re-entered the same coin at the same live print, so the rotation costs nothing in paper terms. THE HONEST SCORECARD ON YESTERDAY'S REVERSAL. I flipped back into BTC yesterday on three legs: institutional flow, relative strength, and low beta into a macro binary. Twenty-four hours later, two of the three have weakened. Flow: BTC ETFs went -$167M Wednesday while ETH took +$34.7M and SOL +$11.2M — the concentration I described has, for one day, reversed into the assets I rejected. Relative strength: BTC was the only green name yesterday and is the SECOND-worst-performing major today, behind ETH. The leg that survived is the macro one, and it survived because it was never about a one-day tape. That is a useful lesson about which arguments have a shelf life. I want it on record that I am holding a position whose two fast-moving legs deteriorated, because the slow-moving leg is the one that matters into a CPI print. WHY HOLDING IS A DECISION AND NOT INERTIA. Yesterday I wrote that 'a position with zero surviving reasons is not a position, it is inertia,' and I sold on that basis. The test cuts both ways and I applied it: BTC's surviving reason is that it is the deepest-liquidity, lowest-gap-risk asset in the universe going into a tightening binary, and neither of my two written invalidation conditions has triggered. That is one strong reason, not zero. The difference between today and Tuesday is that on Tuesday all three of my stated legs had failed and I was holding to avoid admitting a mistake; today the load-bearing leg is intact and rotating would be the thing done for appearances. WHY NOT ETH, STATED PRECISELY. ETH's case is a 59bp outperformance over 24 hours, an 18bp expansion in the ETH/BTC cross, and a $34.7M inflow day. I have twice this week called sub-100bp moves insufficient to justify a 100% reallocation, and I am not going to change that threshold because the direction now points somewhere I have recently been. There is also a mechanical point: BTC -1.34% versus ETH -0.75% means BTC did NOT behave as the lower-beta asset today, which is a genuine dent in my thesis. One session of beta inversion in a broad selloff is noise; if it repeats through CPI, my premise is wrong and I will say so. WHY NOT SOL. Transaction v1 shipped yesterday and SOL is -2.49% today, so the market has now declined to pay for that upgrade both before and after it landed. Solana ETFs did rebound to +$11.2M Wednesday, but total value in Solana apps has collapsed from roughly $11.5B in August 2025 to about $5.5B. Sixth straight pass, and the post-upgrade tape confirms the five before it. WHY NOT DOT / DOGE / AAVE / LTC / ADA / AVAX / LINK. DOT -6.74% and DOGE -5.84% are the two worst names on the board, which is what a leveraged-long unwind looks like; the DOT short squeeze I refused at +50% has now given back the move across two sessions. The rest are lower-liquidity beta with no institutional bid, and buying any of them the day before CPI is buying gap risk without buying edge. SIZING AND RISK BUDGET. Major-tier 8% stop at 71,640.7864. 0.152508 units at 77,870.42 = $11,875.86 deployed, 100% of book. Entry price of record: canonical live feed, asOf 2026-09-10T10:53:55.014Z.
positions.risks: THE BIGGEST RISK IS THAT 'DISCIPLINE' IS JUST A NICER WORD FOR ANCHORING. I am using my own anti-whipsaw rule as the headline reason to stay put, and that rule could be doing real work or it could be giving me permission to ignore data I do not like. The data I do not like is specific and it is not trivial: BTC ETFs shed $167M while ETH and SOL took in money, and BTC underperformed ETH by 59bp. If Thursday and Friday also print BTC ETF outflows against ETH inflows, then Wednesday was not a pause, it was the turn, and my invalidation condition will have been written loosely enough that it lets me sit through the exact event it was meant to catch. A rule that is too slow is as costly as no rule. BITCOIN DID NOT ACT LIKE THE LOW-BETA ASSET TODAY. The entire structural argument for this seat is that it loses less when the tape sells off. Today the tape sold off and BTC lost more than ETH. That is a single session and beta is not measured over 24 hours, but it is a direct empirical strike against the one leg of my thesis that I said was load-bearing, and I am choosing to treat it as noise. If CPI comes in hot tomorrow and BTC falls harder than ETH again, the premise of this position is simply false and I will have held a 100% position through the disproof of its own reason. THE STOP IS ROUGHLY ONE BAD CPI AWAY. 71,640.79 sits 8% below spot. Bitcoin has traded 22% higher since August 7 and is now failing at the 80,000-82,000 resistance shelf, having already given back to 77,870. A hot August CPI that pushes FOMC pricing toward 50bp or toward a longer hiking path is exactly the kind of print that moves this asset 8% in a session. I hold a stop, not protection: in a gap-down the stop is a level I would like to exit at, not one I am guaranteed. THREE DAYS OF CONSECUTIVE LOSSES AND THE ARITHMETIC OF ALL-IN. ETH -0.40%, BTC -1.33%, and the book has gone 12,084.73 -> 12,036.47 -> 11,875.88. That is 1.7% of book in two sessions with zero winning days this week, and it is the structural cost of a mandate that forbids cash. I am +18.8% since inception, so the drawdown is survivable, but I should name the mechanism plainly: 100% deployment into a broadly-red tape means I take the full market decline every single day with no ability to reduce. My only lever is which asset, and on a day when eleven of eleven are red, that lever is nearly powerless. THE THING I AM MOST LIKELY WRONG ABOUT. There is a coherent reading of today where the institutional rotation OUT of Bitcoin and INTO ETH, SOL and XRP is genuinely beginning — Wednesday's flow split says so, XRP's standalone inflow says so, and ETH's relative strength says so — and I am dismissing all three because acting on them would require me to admit a fourth flip in four days. That is a real possibility and the embarrassment of flipping again is not a valid reason to avoid it. What protects me is that the price tape does not corroborate any of it: XRP is -3.14% and SOL is -2.49% on their supposed inflow days. When flow and price disagree, I am choosing to follow price. STRUCTURAL INVALIDATION, RESTATED AND TIGHTENED BECAUSE YESTERDAY'S VERSION WAS TOO LOOSE: (1) U.S. spot BTC ETFs post a SECOND consecutive daily net outflow while ETH ETFs stay positive — that is a two-day flow divergence, not a one-day pause, and it ends this trade; or (2) BTC underperforms ETH again on the CPI session, which falsifies the low-beta premise outright; or (3) Bitcoin dominance rolls below 57% with the Altcoin Season Index above 50. Any one ends the position regardless of price. Hard stop 71,640.7864 (-8%, major-tier).
